The '''2012–13 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team''' represented [[Syracuse University]] in the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The head coach, [[Jim Boeheim]], served for his 37th year. The team played its home games at the [[Carrier Dome]] in [[Syracuse, New York]] and was a member of the [[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|Big East Conference]].  This team reached the [[NCAA Men's Division I Final Four appearances by school|Final Four]] for the fifth time in program history.

==Preseason outlook==

Syracuse began the season ranked #9 in the [[Coaches' Poll]] and the [[Ap poll#College basketball|AP poll]], the second-highest ranking among Big East teams behind Louisville.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2012/10/17/usa-today-sports-mens-basketball-poll/1638933/|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=October 17, 2012|title=USA TODAY Sports men's basketball coaches poll|accessdate=2012-10-17}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/8555195/indiana-hoosiers-top-ap-preseason-hoops-poll|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=October 26, 2012|title=Indiana preseason No. 1 in AP poll|access-date=2012-10-26}}</ref> In a poll of Big East coaches, Syracuse was predicted to finish second in the conference.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2012/10/big_east_coaches_make_louisvil.html|publisher=[[The Post-Standard|Syracuse Post-Standard]]|date=October 17, 2012|title=Big East coaches make Louisville the unanimous pick to win league |accessdate=2012-10-17}}</ref> In this same poll, the coaches named [[Brandon Triche]] to their all-Big East second team.  [[C. J. Fair]] received an honorable mention.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2012/10/big_east_coaches_name_louisvil.html|publisher=Syracuse Post-Standard|date=October 17, 2012|title=Big East coaches name Louisville's Peyton Siva as preseason player of the year|accessdate=2012-10-17}}</ref>

A poll of writers in Big East cities predicted Syracuse would finish second in the conference.  Triche, Fair and [[Michael Carter-Williams]] were named to the writers' all-Big East second team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2012/10/louisville_tops_big_east_write.html|publisher=Syracuse Post-Standard|date=October 16, 2012|title=Louisville tops Big East writers' poll; Cardinals dominate all-league teams|accessdate=2012-10-17}}</ref>

==Roster changes==
[[File:2012–13 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team.jpg|thumb|The 2012–2013 team at the [[Georgia Dome]]]]
Syracuse returned five players that had significant playing time last season (three players that earned starts and two that came off the bench), while losing four significant contributors.

Syracuse graduated two players that started every game during the previous season:  senior point guard [[Scoop Jardine]] and senior forward [[Kris Joseph]]. Sophomore guard [[Dion Waiters]], who averaged 24 minutes per game in the 2011–12 season, left school early to enter the NBA draft, as did sophomore center [[Fab Melo]], who was a starter before the university ruled him academically ineligible toward the end of the season.

The starting line-up for the first half of the current season featured three players who started games in the previous season: senior guard Brandon Triche, junior forward C.J. Fair and sophomore forward [[Rakeem Christmas]].

Sophomore guard Michael Carter-Williams, who did not start in the previous season, but played an average of 10 minutes per game, entered the starting line-up in the 2012–13 season, along with true freshman forward [[DaJuan Coleman]].

Nine players have earned more than 10 minutes per game in the first half of the season. Senior [[James Southerland]] was averaging 26 minutes per game through 16 games before Syracuse University ruled him ineligible in January 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2013/01/syracuse_senior_james_southerl.html|title = Syracuse senior James Southerland ineligible; status for season unknown|date = 13 January 2013}}</ref> The three other players who have been playing off the bench for the team this season are redshirt freshman guard Trevor Cooney, freshman forward Jerami Grant and junior center Baye Moussa Keita. Keita also played off the bench last season.

By January of the 2012–13 season, more than halfway through, Syracuse was playing with just seven scholarship players due to Dajuan Coleman's knee injury and James Southerland's suspension. Coleman was Syracuse's starting center at the beginning of the season and Southerland led the team in three point scoring coming off the bench before his suspension. Head coach Boeheim said he thinks a rotation of seven or eight players is enough to compete.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/ncaa/men/gameflash/2013/02/04/78878_preview.html | archive-url=https://archive.today/20130215174705/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/ncaa/men/gameflash/2013/02/04/78878_preview.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=February 15, 2013 | work=CNN | title=Notre Dame vs. Syracuse}}</ref>

==Jim Boeheim milestones==

Jim Boeheim became only the third coach to win 900 men's [[NCAA Division I]] games on December 17, 2012, when Syracuse defeated [[2012–13 Detroit Titans men's basketball team|Detroit]], 72–68.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2012/12/syracuse_coach_jim_boeheim_rea.html|publisher=Syracuse Post-Standard|date=December 17, 2012|title=Syracuse coach Jim Boeheim reaches the 900-win plateau|accessdate=2012-12-17}}</ref>  On December 31, 2012, Jim Boeheim won his 902nd game tying [[Bob Knight]] for second-most men's NCAA Division I victories with a 96–62 win over [[2012–13 Central Connecticut Blue Devils men's basketball team|Central Connecticut]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2012/12/syracuse_downs_central_connect.html|publisher=Syracuse Post-Standard|date=December 31, 2012|title=Syracuse downs Central Connecticut State; Jim Boeheim ties Bob Knight with 902 wins|accessdate=2013-01-01}}</ref>  Boeheim passed Knight to gain sole possession of second place behind [[Mike Krzyzewski]] when Syracuse defeated [[2012–13 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]] 78–53 on January 2, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2013/01/syracuse_routs_rutgers_as_jim.html|publisher=Syracuse Post-Standard|date=January 2, 2013|title=Syracuse routs Rutgers as Jim Boeheim passes Bob Knight on all-time coaching wins list|accessdate=2013-01-02}}</ref>
